prompt: compare slaes data of our data and seattle store.
title: Sales Data Comparison
summary: Compare our sales data with the Seattle store’s sales data. Highlight key differences, trends, and any notable performance gaps.
executed_sql_queries:
SELECT
  s.store_id,
  s.store_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS number_of_orders,
  COALESCE(SUM(oi.total_amount), 0) AS total_sales_amount,
  COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS total_units_sold,
  CASE
    WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE COALESCE(SUM(oi.total_amount), 0) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)
  END AS average_order_value
FROM retail.stores s
LEFT JOIN retail.orders o
  ON s.store_id = o.store_id
LEFT JOIN retail.order_items oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
 AND o.store_id = oi.store_id
GROUP BY s.store_id, s.store_name
ORDER BY s.store_name;

WITH monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
    s.store_name,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS sales_amount
  FROM retail.orders o
  JOIN retail.order_items oi
    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
   AND o.store_id = oi.store_id
  JOIN retail.stores s
    ON o.store_id = s.store_id
  GROUP BY 1, 2
)
SELECT
  month,
  CASE
    WHEN store_name = 'Zava Retail Seattle' THEN 'Zava Retail Seattle'
    ELSE 'All accessible stores overall'
  END AS comparison_group,
  SUM(sales_amount) AS sales_amount
FROM monthly_sales
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

SELECT c.category_name,
       SUM(oi.total_amount) AS sales_amount,
       SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN retail.order_items oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN retail.products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN retail.categories c
  ON p.category_id = c.category_id
GROUP BY c.category_name
ORDER BY sales_amount DESC;
